title: Characterization of feeding practices for premature infants in the Department of Neonatology and Pediatric Intensive Care Medicine at Halle University Hospital (2021–2023), with a special focus on guideline adherence
summary: This retrospective study aims to examine whether premature infants at Halle University Hospital (Saale) are fed in accordance with the recommendations of various guidelines in terms of energy requirements and macronutrient requirements during their inpatient stay in the Department of Neonatology and Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine, and whether this ensures optimal weight and growth development. Guideline adherence will be assessed for the 2014 S3 guideline of the DGEM, the 2022 European ESPGHAN guideline and the 2024 internal guideline of the Department of Neonatology and Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine at Halle (Saale) University Hospital.
conditions: Disorders related to short gestation and low birth weight, not elsewhere classified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Premature birth before completion of the 37th week of pregnancy and inpatient stay in the Neonatology and Paediatric Intensive Care Unit of the Department of Operative and Conservative Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Paediatrics II, University Hospital Halle
Exclusion criteria:
- Congenital anomalies: chromosomal abnormalities, congenital cyanotic heart disease and anomalies of the gastrointestinal system
- Metabolic diseases, kidney, liver or endocrine disorders
- Severe genetic disorders that impair growth or neurological development
- Incurable diseases in which life-sustaining measures have been limited or withheld 
- Cerebral haemorrhages of grade III or higher
- Abdominal surgery leading to malabsorption, e.g. involving intestinal resection
- Surgery due to necrotising enterocolitis with intestinal resection
- Surgery due to congenital anomalies with intestinal resection, e.g. Hirschsprung's disease, small bowel atresia or oesophageal atresia 
- Surgery due to mechanical ileus, volvulus or intussusception with bowel resection
- Surgery due to spontaneous intestinal perforation
- Multiple abdominal surgeries, e.g. in cases of complicated omphalocele repair or stoma repair in Hirschsprung's disease
